chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said to me, “Have you recognized your Imam?” He said: I said, “Yes, by Allah, before I departed from al-Kūfah.” So he said, “That is sufficient for you, then.”

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar; the Imam speaking in the narration
key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: your Imam; the divinely appointed leader whose recognition is being asked about
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: al-Kūfah; the city mentioned as the place from which the speaker departed
key_terms.حَسْبُكَ: it is sufficient for you; it is enough for your need in this matter
key_terms.عَرَفْتَ: you recognized; you came to know with acknowledgement

ai.seo_question: Why is recognizing the Imam considered sufficient in this hadith from al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the necessity of recognizing the Imam. The statement of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) indicates that once true recognition of the Imam is attained, that recognition itself is a sufficient foundational matter for the believer.
